subject: Audit log onboarding questions and BYOK/retention constraints - NovaMed
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novamed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit logs + BYOK question for NovaMed pilot

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our security team pushed back on two items we need clarified before committing to the pilot:

1) Audit log granularity: They want a sample of the exact event schema (timestamps, actor id, request/response metadata, model id, token-level redaction markers) and confirmation that logs can be exported to our SIEM.

2) Keys & retention: Our standard is customer-managed keys (BYOK) with a maximum 30-day retention for raw user content logs. Can Redwood support BYOK for the inference audit stream and a configurable retention policy limited to 30 days?

Attached is the onboarding request form they asked us to fill out with high-level answers — can you confirm what you can support and what requires an exception?

Looking to get this back to InfoSec by Wed.

Thanks,
Liam

Subject: Re: Audit logs + BYOK question for NovaMed pilot

Hi Liam — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Quick acknowledgement: we can get a concrete answer, and I've started a short triage with Marissa and Priyom to map product impacts. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we escalate to engineering:

- When you say "export to our SIEM", do you need a push integration (S3/HTTPS) or do you prefer us to provide daily batches you ingest?
- For "raw user content logs": do you mean full request/response payloads (pre-redaction) or metadata-only (events + hashes)?
- Is NovaMed expecting the KMS to be in their cloud tenant (customer-managed CMEK) or simply that they hold the master key offline and we accept wrapped keys?

I've attached a short triage matrix that maps our likely implementation paths to impact (engineering effort, security review, timeline). Please review and confirm; if you prefer a quick call we can set one up tomorrow afternoon.

Outcome we're aiming for: either (A) standard-config BYOK + 30d retention supported out-of-the-box, or (B) documented exception path with explicit list of changes and estimated timeline. We'll need InfoSec sign-off for B.

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa will flag any product constraints (schema changes, export hooks).
- Priyom will assess infra work for BYOK + export connectors.
- I will draft the exception framing if needed and own the timeline with you.

Best,

Subject: Re: Audit logs + BYOK question for NovaMed pilot

Thanks all — 10am PT works. To answer Soojin's clarifying questions briefly:

- SIEM integration: push to our S3 bucket is preferred (we already have ingestion there).
- Raw user content logs: InfoSec requires request + response payloads for a 30-day window; after 30 days they should be permanently deleted. They will accept token-level redaction if we can demonstrate equivalence, but prefer full payloads for initial audit.
- KMS: NovaMed operates a customer KMS in their AWS account. They expect CMEK support (keystore in their tenant) or an HSM-backed wrapped-key flow we can demonstrate.

I've uploaded our completed questionnaire to the portal and attached a PDF copy here. Also linking our compliance portal: https://compliance.novamed.com/pilot/12345

See you on the call.

Liam

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Audit logs + BYOK question for NovaMed pilot

Quick notes and internal asks following the call:

Decision checkpoints identified
- BYOK path: prioritized to support CMEK in customer AWS account. Priyom: can we confirm if we can accept customer CMK ARN + do key wrapping flows, or will we require a dedicated connector?
- Retention model: implement configurable retention at the stream level with enforcement hook to delete raw payloads after X days. Target for NovaMed: X=30 but make it configurable for enterprise customers.
- Export: S3 push with ACLs to their bucket acceptable; need S3 delivery SLA and encryption-in-transit confirmation from infra.

Product asks for roadmap/estimates (Marissa)
- Small schema change to include request_id and redaction markers (low effort, small risk).
- Export connector: mid effort (2-3 sprints) to add managed S3 delivery + retry semantics.
- BYOK/CMEK integration: high effort (security review + infra work) — estimate 6-8 weeks for a hardened path, less if we accept wrapped-key prototype.

Action items
- Priyom: draft infra workback with security requirements and runbook for key rotation and revocation (due 2026-07-08).
- Marissa: prioritize a small schema PR and doc PR for retention and redaction options (due 2026-07-06).
- Soojin: prepare exception framing if by July 8 we cannot commit to CMEK; communicate ETA to NovaMed InfoSec and propose wrapped-key POC as interim.

I'll open a short RFC and tag product/security owners. Please add any missing technical blockers or compliance gating items in the RFC.

Thanks team — moving faster on this one since it's timeboxed by the customer's compliance review.

Soojin Lee
Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference
